name: Power supply
description: Instead of placing charges, turn a knob: the top deflection plate is connected to a power supply (yellow frame). Click the plate to switch it on, and set its potential with the slider in the panel. A positive plate pushes positive ions away, a negative one pulls them. Bring the beam into the detector.

reality.represents: Deflection set by a power supply's knob

remarks.detail: The sideways push grows in proportion to the plate's voltage, its sign with the voltage's: an oscilloscope's deflection works so.

remarks.line: Real plates and their fringe fields
remarks.detail: The electrodes are metal boxes standing on the plane, their surface charge solved exactly (boundary elements): uniform between plates, bulging out past their ends, and rearranging when charges come near, as in a real instrument.
A plate on a supply sits at its voltage whatever charge that takes; a real supply has an internal resistance and leads, and charging a plate takes a current for a while (the Circuits arc).

Everything is symmetric about the plane z = 0, so the particle never leaves it. A real beam also has a width across the plane, where the same fields act differently (focusing in the plane can defocus across it).
